collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The old one-eyed dog everyone feeds has fallen sick: try to treat it, or let it rest in peace.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The old one-eyed dog that wanders the village, eating everyone's scraps, has stopped eating and lies under the meeting hut all day. (subject) is beside it. (friend) says the healers might help, or it might only frighten the old dog more. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The healers give the dog a little broth and a bitter herb. It eats the broth and refuses the herb. For a week it seems better. Then it lies down for good, in the sun, with (subject) beside it. The village buries it under the fig tree.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) sits with the dog every day, in the shade, stroking its ears. It wags its tail weakly. One morning it is gone, peacefully. (subject) chooses the spot under the fig tree. Half the village comes to the burial.
